text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A meeting between Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash and Britain's envoy Sir David Hannay was called off after Denktash sought recognition for his breakaway state. Richard Holbrooke, appointed U.S. presidential emissary on the Cyprus dispute last week, speaks of a "mini Dayton" on Cyprus.
- Telethon for the muscular dystrophy foundation nets 300,000 pounds ($503,500).
- Newly appointed U.S. special envoy on Cyprus Richard Holbrooke says the tense situation on the island could explode at any moment.
- The Cyprus Football Association blames the Turkish Cypriots over axed soccer matches.
- David Hannay speaks of "convergence" now in views instead of "common ground". Denktash called off a meeting with him.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash shut the door in David Hannay's face because he saw the Cypriot foreign minister and the parliamentary speaker.
- The Cyprus Ports Authority will face a liquidity squeeze in the future because of the high levels of investments made in Limassol port, says Communications and Works Minister Leondios Ierodiakonou.
- The Cyprus Ports Authority starts sinking. Tug operators are threatening strikes to protest the change in the job description plans of a port official.
